pr_title: Improve `AStarGrid2D` performance when jumping is enabled
pr_body:
fixes #91367

On sparse grids, enabling jumping can now increase performance 5x, which should be more than 10x faster than before, as jumping unintentionally used to decrease performance instead.

[AStarGrid_jumping_Performance.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/15890711/AStarGrid_jumping_Performance.zip)
pr_comments:
I see some inconsistencies with current pathfinding:

At this commit:
![изображение](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/3036176/879e931e-34dc-425b-b494-ecd3fa1c8eca)

At master:

I notice this PR and #85965 (both ready to merge) will conflict, so one would need to be merged first and the other rebased. But I wanted to take the opportunity to get both checked in parallel, I'm not familiar with AStar implementation but I wonder if there's overlap in what those two optimizations aim to solve, and thus whether they will combine well or not.

CC @ershn @godotengine/navigation

> I wonder if there's overlap in what those two optimizations aim to solve

I'd say they do exist in separate spaces, but I'd have to check whether this specific optimization is still significantly faster compared to improved general performance from the other PR
On a second look, the linked PR appears to be completely separate. I am also not seeing any conflicts with their changes

@akien-mga
This should not create any conflict with the other linked PR. This PR here touches the AStar classes (aka AStar2D/3D/Grid) and those live in their own silo in core primarily maintained by core, while the other PR touched things in the navigation module that is separate.

Seems like the rebase went wrong in this PR, I'll try to fix it up.

Regarding the conflict, I thought there was one as I tried merging both PRs locally and the build was failing, because this PR removes the `solid` member in the `Point` struct, which is still used. But it might just be this PR which was outdated and not handling more recent additions of usage of `solid`, I wrongly assumed this was related to the other PR.
Thanks! And congrats for your first merged Godot contribution :tada:

issue_context.title: AStarGrid2D with jumping_enabled is significantly slower than with it disabled.
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

Tested in 4.2.2 stable

### System information

Windows 10, Godot 4.2.2 stable

### Issue description

The Docs description for enabling jumping AStarGrid2D on states that is intended to speed up the algorithm, but testing showed it slowing down the calculations by a significant amount, around 4-7 times slower.
https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_astargrid2d.html#class-astargrid2d-property-jumping-enabled


No jumping
large distance with many obstacles- average 21.42
large distance with few obstacles- average 8.35
small distance - average 0.32

Jumping
large distance with many obstacles-average 149.41
large distance with few obstacles- average 33.76
small distance - average 1.52



### Steps to reproduce

Open the Minimal reproduction project 
Use the `@export` variables to change the path distance and toggle jumping.
Use the run speed test button to print the speed of the function to the consol.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[AStarGridPerformance.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/15168192/AStarGridPerformance.zip)
comments: ~I suspect that algorithm should be faster on open-space with low amount of obstacles rather than high.~ Nvm, it's really slower, strange... The other assumption that  it currently uses a recursion, and this might be slower than without (but significantly easier to develop).
I am encountering the same issue, if no one is working on this right now, I would like to try working on a fix.

> I would like to try working on a fix.

You are welcome, that code was a painful to create and maintain.

The combination of branching and recursion definitely appears to play a large part in the lack of performance here. Some recursion can simply be rewritten to loops, but others need to perform multiple different jump checks themselves. I'll mostly be figuring out a way to reduce unnecessary branching in a way that is still somewhat maintainable :)
